quizName: DMV Practice Test #16 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If you get a flat tire while riding, what should you do?

options.text: Hold the handgrips firmly and do not use the brakes.
Shift your weight toward the good wheel and brake normally.
Brake on the good wheel and pull off the road immediately.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handgrips firmly and do not use the brakes.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat while riding, grip the handlebars firmly and stay in a straight line. Only brake if you know which tire is flat. Once the motorcycle slows down, pull off the road.

questions.question: When making a U-turn, what should you do with the brakes?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes at the same time.
Do not use the front brake because it could cause the bike to tip over.
Use the front brake to keep the motorcycle stable.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the front brake because it could cause the bike to tip over.
questions.explanation: Do not use the front brake during a U-turn because it can make the bike tip over. Use only the rear brake to slow down.

questions.question: When passing a truck on a two-lane road, when should you return to your lane?

options.text: When you can see the entire front of the truck in your rearview mirror.
As soon as the truck is behind you.
When you feel you have enough space.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the entire front of the truck in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Return to your lane only when you can see the entire front of the truck in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: When passing a row of parked cars, which part of the lane should you ride in?

options.text: The left side of the lane.
Wherever you feel most comfortable.
The right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left side of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride on the left side of the lane. This position helps you avoid dangers like opening car doors, people stepping out between cars, and cars pulling out of spaces. Always be ready to change position based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: In Idaho, at what blood alcohol content (BAC) is someone under 21 considered legally intoxicated?

options.text: 0.02 percent or higher.
0.04 percent or higher.
0.08 percent or higher.
0.1 percent or higher.

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.02 percent or higher.
questions.explanation: In Idaho, drivers under 21 are legally intoxicated at 0.02 percent BAC or higher. Drivers 21 and older are legally intoxicated at 0.08 percent BAC or higher. Driving while intoxicated is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: If parked vehicles are on your right and there is no oncoming traffic, which part of your lane should you ride in?

options.text: The left portion of your lane.
The right portion of your lane.
The center of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane. This helps you avoid dangers like opening car doors and people stepping out between vehicles. If there is oncoming traffic, stay in the center to have more space around you.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: The light is about to turn red.
The light is about to turn green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light is about to turn red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light warns that the light will turn red soon. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection, continue through.

questions.question: What is the key to making a quick turn?

options.text: Shift your weight quickly.
Turn the handlebars quickly.
Lean the motorcycle quickly in the direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean the motorcycle quickly in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: To make a quick turn, lean the motorcycle quickly in the direction you want to go. The sharper the turn, the more the bike must lean.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When the pavement is slippery.
When traffic is light.
When you can see through the vehicles ahead to check traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the pavement is slippery.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when it takes longer to stop. This includes slippery pavement, when you cannot see ahead, or when traffic is heavy. Use at least a four-second following distance in these situations.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Right lane ends
Left lane ends
Traffic control device ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Right lane ends
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They warn drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the right lane ends.

questions.question: How should you carry a load on your motorcycle?

options.text: Over the rear axle.
On the gas tank in front of you.
Piled against the back of the seat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over the rear axle.
questions.explanation: Loads must be kept over or in front of the rear axle. Only experienced riders should carry loads.

questions.question: How should you position your body when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Hold yourself up with your arms.
Use your arms to steer the motorcycle.
Stretch to reach the handgrips.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your arms to steer the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Position yourself so your arms steer the motorcycle, not hold you up. Your elbows should bend slightly when holding the handgrips.

questions.question: What is the best formation for a group of motorcycle riders?

options.text: Single-file formation.
Riding in pairs.
Staggered formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: Staggered formation.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation lets riders stay close together while giving each rider enough space to stop safely.

questions.question: What does a solid white line on the side of the road mean?

options.text: No parking is allowed.
The right edge of a traffic lane.
Traffic must merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right edge of a traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line marks the right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.question: What is the minimum following distance for a motorcyclist in normal conditions?

options.text: Two seconds.
Three seconds.
Four seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds.
questions.explanation: Keep a two-second distance behind the vehicle ahead in normal conditions. Use more distance if conditions are poor.

questions.question: How should you cross angled railroad tracks?

options.text: Use the shoulder to slow down before crossing.
Walk your motorcycle across the tracks.
Ride straight within your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride straight within your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride straight across angled tracks within your lane. Changing your angle can send you into another lane and cause a crash.

questions.question: What usually causes the front wheel and handlebars to shake suddenly?

options.text: Incorrect tire pressure or uneven loading.
Front wheel not tightened properly to the frame.
Hitting an object with the front tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Incorrect tire pressure or uneven loading.
questions.explanation: This shaking usually comes from improper loading, wrong accessories, or incorrect tire pressure.

questions.question: What should you NOT do when approaching an intersection?

options.text: Position yourself to be more visible.
Speed up to cross quickly.
Prepare your clutch and brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to cross quickly.
questions.explanation: Choose a visible lane position. Prepare your clutch and brakes to react faster. Slow down as you approach. Avoid sudden speed or position changes that confuse other drivers.

questions.question: What helps you control a motorcycle well?

options.text: Use your arms to hold yourself up.
Keep your knees against the gas tank.
Sit with your arms straight when reaching the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank.
questions.explanation: Sit so your arms steer the motorcycle, not hold you up. Your elbows should bend slightly. Keep your knees against the gas tank to help balance.

questions.question: What should you do when riding at night?

options.text: Ride on the shoulder of the road.
Decrease your following distance.
Increase your following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance at night. Slow down and adjust your lane position as needed.

questions.question: While riding, you should wear:

options.text: Hearing protection to protect your ears from engine and wind noise.
A helmet to protect your hearing.
A baseball cap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hearing protection to protect your ears from engine and wind noise.
questions.explanation: Engine and wind noise can damage your hearing over time, even with a full-face helmet. Wear hearing protection to prevent this damage.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing your motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Swerve around the dog.
Slow down and let the dog get close, then speed up and ride away.
Park and wait for the dog to lose interest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the dog get close, then speed up and ride away.
questions.explanation: Dogs often chase motorcycles. If a dog chases you, slow down and approach it. Then accelerate quickly to leave it behind.

questions.question: A person with a minimum blood alcohol content (BAC) of ____ is considered intoxicated.

options.text: 0.02 percent
0.04 percent
0.08 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: In Virginia, a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher means a person is intoxicated. Intoxicated drivers cannot legally operate a motor vehicle.

questions.question: A motorcyclist should avoid obstacles on the road. If you cannot avoid an obstacle, you should:

options.text: Speed up before hitting the object.
Stay seated so the seat absorbs some impact.
Hit the obstacle at a 90-degree angle if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hit the obstacle at a 90-degree angle if possible.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid an obstacle, slow down and hit it at as close to a 90-degree angle as possible.

questions.question: When being passed, where should a motorcyclist position their motorcycle in the lane?

options.text: The right
The center
The left

questions.correctAnswerText: The center
questions.explanation: Stay in the center of your lane when being passed from behind or by an oncoming vehicle. This keeps both you and the other driver safe.
